Also, during the year NCLT (Ahmedabad) cases under IBC Section 7 (Stratmont Coal and Commodity Private Limited & Vatsal Agrawal) and Section 9 (M/s. Tejomay Exim Corporation), plus a case by MSTC Limited, were all dismissed. Read in the Directors' Report, item 40 (Significant and Material Orders).

risks.note: The Company does not own the premises where its registered office is situated; a leave & license agreement is in place, and any termination or dispute over this lease/rental agreement may adversely affect business operations and results.
The Company operates in a highly fragmented and competitive industry, and increased competition or concentration of customers and suppliers may reduce revenues, profit margins, or market share.
risks.risk: Fragmented, competitive industry with customer/supplier concentration exposure

risks.note: Business is dependent on the ability to operate the single manufacturing facility at enhanced capacity; disruptions from equipment breakdown, industrial accidents, natural or man-made disasters, workforce disruptions, regulatory approval delays, fire, machinery failure, or power/water supply issues could adversely affect the ability to manufacture products.

The steel industry has a high proportion of fixed costs and is subject to volatility in raw material and energy prices; limitations or disruptions in raw material supply could adversely affect profitability.
risks.risk: Raw material price and supply volatility

risks.note: There have been past instances of delayed disclosures and inadvertent incorrect/incomplete factual disclosures under SEBI Listing Regulations, including delayed filings under Regulation 23(9) and Regulation 30, incorrect categorization of Promoter and Promoter Group under Regulation 31, and delayed compliance under Regulation 74(5) of the SEBI Depositories and Participants Regulations; such non-compliance has drawn penalties, warnings and show cause notices.

Non-compliance with increasingly stringent regulatory and environmental norms may result in liabilities and reputational damage; contravention of regulatory approvals applicable to the manufacturing facility may require the Company to cease or limit production.
risks.risk: Regulatory approval and environmental compliance risk

risks.note: The Company cannot assure there will be no future work disruptions from disputes with employees or labour involved in the manufacturing facility, which could hinder regular operating activities.

Violation of safety standards, unsafe acts and conditions may lead to Lost Time Injuries (LTIs) or fatalities, resulting in stoppage of operations, loss of personnel, and damage to assets and reputation.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company does not own the premises where its registered office is situated; a leave & license agreement is in place, and any termination or dispute over this lease/rental agreement may adversely affect business operations and results.
- The Company operates in a highly fragmented and competitive industry, and increased competition or concentration of customers and suppliers may reduce revenues, profit margins, or market share.
- Business is dependent on the ability to operate the single manufacturing facility at enhanced capacity; disruptions from equipment breakdown, industrial accidents, natural or man-made disasters, workforce disruptions, regulatory approval delays, fire, machinery failure, or power/water supply issues could adversely affect the ability to manufacture products.
- The steel industry has a high proportion of fixed costs and is subject to volatility in raw material and energy prices; limitations or disruptions in raw material supply could adversely affect profitability.
- There have been past instances of delayed disclosures and inadvertent incorrect/incomplete factual disclosures under SEBI Listing Regulations, including delayed filings under Regulation 23(9) and Regulation 30, incorrect categorization of Promoter and Promoter Group under Regulation 31, and delayed compliance under Regulation 74(5) of the SEBI Depositories and Participants Regulations; such non-compliance has drawn penalties, warnings and show cause notices.
- Non-compliance with increasingly stringent regulatory and environmental norms may result in liabilities and reputational damage; contravention of regulatory approvals applicable to the manufacturing facility may require the Company to cease or limit production.
- The Company cannot assure there will be no future work disruptions from disputes with employees or labour involved in the manufacturing facility, which could hinder regular operating activities.
- Violation of safety standards, unsafe acts and conditions may lead to Lost Time Injuries (LTIs) or fatalities, resulting in stoppage of operations, loss of personnel, and damage to assets and reputation.
